questions.q: What memory cost does activation checkpointing target, which ZeRO and FSDP do not address?
options: The optimizer state's moment buffers
Activations -- the intermediate layer outputs the backward pass needs, which scale with depth, batch size, and sequence length rather than parameter count
The size of the dataset on disk
The size of the model checkpoint file
questions.explain: ZeRO and FSDP shard weights, gradients, and optimizer state. Activations are a separate memory consumer, scaling with depth times batch size times sequence length, independent of how parameters are sharded.

questions.q: What is the core trade-off activation checkpointing makes?
options: It reduces both memory and compute simultaneously with no downside
It discards intermediate activations during the forward pass and recomputes them during the backward pass, trading extra compute time for reduced peak memory
It permanently deletes gradients to save disk space
It reduces the number of layers in the model
questions.explain: Activation checkpointing discards activations after use in the forward pass and recomputes them via a second forward pass when the backward pass needs them -- more compute in exchange for less peak activation memory.

questions.q: In PyTorch's torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint, what does setting use_reentrant=False do?
options: It disables checkpointing entirely
It selects PyTorch's newer, more robust checkpointing implementation, which is the current recommended default over the older reentrant-autograd-based one
It forces the model to run only in fp32
It increases the batch size automatically
questions.explain: use_reentrant=False opts into PyTorch's newer checkpointing implementation, which is more robust than the original reentrant-autograd-based approach and is the currently recommended setting.

questions.q: What is the simplest way to enable activation checkpointing on a Hugging Face Transformers model?
options: Manually rewrite every layer's forward method
Call model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(), or set gradient_checkpointing=True in TrainingArguments/SFTConfig
Switch the optimizer from AdamW to SGD
Reduce the model's hidden size
questions.explain: Hugging Face Transformers exposes activation checkpointing as a single call, model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(), or equivalently as a TrainingArguments/SFTConfig flag, applied automatically at transformer-block granularity.

questions.q: Why is activation checkpointing typically combined with data parallelism and ZeRO/FSDP rather than chosen as an alternative to them?
options: Because it is functionally identical to ZeRO stage 3

Because it targets a completely different part of the memory budget (activations) than those techniques (weights, gradients, optimizer state), so combining them frees up different kinds of memory simultaneously
Because PyTorch requires all four techniques to be used together or none at all
Because activation checkpointing only works without any form of parallelism
questions.explain: Activation checkpointing addresses activation memory, a separate line item from the weights/gradients/optimizer-state memory that data parallelism, ZeRO, and FSDP address, so production configs commonly combine all of them.
